newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-Sumitomo trader Hamanaka arrested for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Sumitomo trader Hamanaka arrested for fraud.

text.p: Japanese prosecutors said on Wednesday that they had arrested Sumitomo Corp's former star copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka on suspicion of fraud in the latest legal action against him.
Hamanaka, already under arrest and in custody on forgery charges, was served a fresh arrest warrant in the Tokyo Detention Centre where he has been held since October 22.

Sumitomo had filed complaints with the prosecutor's office alleging Hamanaka committed forgery and fraud in connection with off-the-book copper trades that the company blamed for an estimated $2.6 billion loss.
Sumitomo's fraud complaint was filed with prosecutors on Tuesday, the same day prosecutors indicted Hamanaka on four counts of forgery, for which he was arrested last month.

A statement by the prosecutor's office said Hamanaka was suspected of fraudulently procuring about $771 million from a Sumitomo Hong Kong subsidiary, under the false pretext of purchasing copper warrants, in order to cover massive losses in off-the-book copper options transactions with Morgan Guaranty Trust Co of New York.

With Wednesday's fraud charges, Morgan Guaranty joins Credit Lyonnais Rouse and firms from the Merrill Lynch group among those listed in Tokyo prosecutors' statements as counterparties to Hamanaka's alleged off-the-books trading.
Commenting on the arrest, a Sumitomo spokesman said: "We hope the investigative authorities will make clear the truth in this case."
The arrest on fraud charges also allows prosecutors to hold Hamanaka in detention for up to 20 more days.
One of Hamanaka's lawyers said the date for Hamanaka's first trial could be set by the end of this year.
